technologies.name: Farming
technologies.description: Allows you to build farms.
technologies.flavor: The first farmers noticed that seeds thrown into the ground grew again. Thus began the age of settled life.

technologies.name: Mining
technologies.description: Allows you to build mines.
technologies.flavor: People learned to draw stone and ore from the depths of the earth, opening a new era in tools.

technologies.name: Native Metals
technologies.description:
Unlocks the ability to find and gather native metals.
Unlocks metal ores (gold, silver, copper) and metalloids (antimony and arsenic).
Allows you to build the forge.
technologies.flavor: People learned to find and use native metals, which occur in nature in pure form, with no need to smelt them out of ore.

unlock_effects.name: Unlocks the ability to find and gather native metals.

technologies.name: Metallurgy
technologies.description: Allows you to build the smelter and smelt metal out of ore.
technologies.flavor: Mastering metals revolutionized the crafts: copper tools were tougher than stone.

technologies.name: Bronze
technologies.description: Unlocks recipes for bronze and bronze goods.
technologies.flavor: People learned to alloy copper with tin to make bronze, a hard metal for tools and weapons. Bronze became a key material for crafts and warfare.

technologies.name: Iron Processing
technologies.description:
Unlocks recipes for iron and iron goods.
Unlocks the bloomery.
technologies.flavor: People learned to alloy copper with tin to make bronze, a hard metal for tools and weapons. Bronze became a key material for crafts and warfare.

technologies.name: Animal Husbandry
technologies.description: Allows you to build pastures.
technologies.flavor: Taming animals gave people a steady source of meat, milk and hides.

technologies.name: Ceramics
technologies.description: Allows you to build the clay pit and the pottery workshop.
technologies.flavor: Fired clay became humanity's first artificial material, letting people store grain and water.

technologies.name: Beekeeping
technologies.description: Allows you to build the apiary.
technologies.flavor: People learned to tame bees for honey and wax, the only natural sweeteners and the stuff of candles.

technologies.name: Fishing
technologies.description: Allows you to build a dock and fishing boats.
technologies.flavor: Fishing is one of humanity's oldest trades, and the first way to take food from the water.

technologies.name: Wood Processing
technologies.description: Allows you to build forest plots (logging) and the carpenter's workshop (timber → planks).
technologies.flavor: Wood is the oldest building material, and with the first axes people learned to fell trees and saw the trunks into planks.

technologies.name: Irrigation
technologies.description:
Unlocks the ability to grow water-loving crops: rice and taro.
Allows farms and plantations to pass fresh water along a chain (up to 3 hexes).
Allows you to drain marshes.
technologies.flavor: Managing water flows became the key to claiming new lands: irrigation did more than water the fields, it drained waterlogged ground and turned marshes into fertile plains.

unlock_effects.name: Unlocks the ability to grow water-loving crops: rice and taro.

technologies.name: Wheel
technologies.description:
Reduces the effect of distance from the city on the work cost of building improvements by 30%.
Unlocks the Cart Road (road level 2): up to 30 units/sec per section instead of 10.
technologies.flavor: The wheel is one of humanity's greatest inventions, and it changed trade and war.

unlock_effects.name: Unlocks the Cart Road (road level 2): 30 units/sec per section.

technologies.name: Plow
technologies.description: +50% to resource production on farms.
technologies.flavor: A plow yoked to oxen made it possible to work heavy soils and raised yields.

technologies.name: Masonry
technologies.description: Allows you to build the quarry and the mason's workshop.
technologies.flavor: The skill of laying stone made it possible to build sturdy buildings that outlived centuries.

technologies.name: Cheese Making
technologies.description: Allows you to build the dairy: raw milk → cheese.
technologies.flavor: Cheese kept milk for months, becoming an important winter supply.

technologies.name: Leatherworking
technologies.description: Allows you to build the tanner's house: hides → leather.
technologies.flavor: Tanning gave people a tough, flexible material for clothing, footwear and gear.

technologies.name: Writing
technologies.description: Allows you to build libraries.
technologies.flavor: Clay tablets became the first carrier of information, letting people pass knowledge across the centuries.

technologies.name: Weaving
technologies.description: Allows you to build the weaver's house: various materials → clothes.
technologies.flavor: The loom turned wool and flax into cloth, from which clothes were sewn.

technologies.name: Oil Making
technologies.description: Allows you to build the hand oil press: seeds, fruits and other parts of oil crops → vegetable oil.
technologies.flavor: Vegetable oil became an important food and a source of light.

technologies.name: Soap Making
technologies.description: Allows you to build the soapmaker's house: vegetable oil and soda → soap.
technologies.flavor: By mixing fat with lye, people got soap, the first step toward hygiene and medicine.

technologies.name: Fermentation
technologies.description: Allows you to build the brewer's house. Unlocks recipes for brewing beer, pulque and sake.
technologies.flavor: Fermentation let people turn grain and fruit into alcohol, drunk in rituals and in daily life.

technologies.name: Mead Making
technologies.description: Unlocks recipes for brewing mead.
technologies.flavor: Mead is the oldest alcohol, brewed from honey and water.

technologies.name: Jewelry
technologies.description: Unlocks recipes for making jewelry out of metals.
technologies.flavor: Working precious stones and metals turned the craft into art.

technologies.name: Winegrowing
technologies.description: Allows you to build the vineyard.
technologies.flavor: The grape is one of the oldest crops, from which people learned to make wine, a drink for feasts and rituals.

technologies.name: Winemaking
technologies.description: Allows you to build the winemaker's house: grapes → wine.
technologies.flavor: Wine was made from grapes: it was a drink for feasts and rituals, and it also kept the perishable grapes from spoiling.

technologies.name: Plantations
technologies.description: Specialized farming: growing cash crops. Allows you to build plantations.
technologies.flavor: Plantations made it possible to grow olives and citrus in bulk, providing valuable goods and oils.

technologies.name: Soda Extraction
technologies.description: Allows you to build the quarry for soda extraction.
technologies.flavor: People noticed that the white crust on the shores of salt lakes cleanses and bleaches wonderfully. So began the extraction of soda, a valuable mineral without which neither glassmaking nor soapmaking is possible.

technologies.name: Glassmaking
technologies.description: Allows you to build the glassmaker's house: sand and soda → glass.
technologies.flavor: For centuries potters watched sand and alkali turn in their kilns into a shining crust of glass. Then one day someone had the idea of doing it on purpose. Glassmaking became more than an accident: it became a deliberate craft. The new material changed the world: beads, amulets, and later tableware and windows. Transparency became a symbol of enlightenment.

technologies.name: Rope Making
technologies.description: Allows you to build the ropemaker's house: fibers → ropes.
technologies.flavor: Ropes became an important material for building, sailing and farming, letting people bind, haul and hoist loads.

technologies.name: Bitumen Extraction
technologies.description: Allows you to build the tar pit and the tar distillery: bitumen → tar.
technologies.flavor: Bitumen became an important material for waterproofing, and for making glue and fuel.

technologies.name: Salt Extraction
technologies.description: Unlocks salt extraction in salt deposits (on the surface of salt lakes and in salt mines) and the salt pond.
technologies.flavor: Salt became an important product for preserving food.

technologies.name: Sericulture
technologies.description: Allows you to build the silkmaker's house: cocoons → silk.
technologies.flavor: Silk became a valuable material for clothing and trade, opening new possibilities for crafts and the economy.

technologies.name: Limestone Burning
technologies.description: Allows you to build the lime kilns: limestone → lime.
technologies.flavor: Burning limestone in kilns made lime possible, a key building material and an ingredient for making cement.

technologies.name: Money
technologies.description: Allows you to build the Market city building.
technologies.flavor: The idea of value and exchange led to money, the basis of trade and city growth.

technologies.name: Canals
technologies.description: Allows you to build canals to bring water to remote areas.
technologies.flavor: Canals let people manage water flows, improving irrigation and opening new routes for trade.

technologies.name: Dyeing
technologies.description: Allows you to extract various dyes from organic and inorganic materials.
technologies.flavor: Dyeing cloth and pottery with various dyes is one of the oldest crafts.
